invariants: tenant and permission clauses are generated from authenticated identity and execute in filter context
live traversal uses search_after with alert_id as a stable deterministic tie-breaker
consistent traversal uses a bounded PIT and never reports timed-out or failed shards as a complete result
signed cursors bind tenant, normalized filters, sort, page size, traversal mode and expiry
signed cursors bind the resolved physical index-set digest; live traversal rejects alias drift while PIT retains frozen shards
legacy from and size fields remain available only for the controlled shallow result window after cutover

data.migration: publish the default-off cursor contract, validate alerts-v2 aliases, shadow query identities and latency, then canary the runtime flag while retaining legacy shallow requests

negative_tests: cross-tenant signed cursor is rejected before OpenSearch access
cursor replay with changed filters, sort, size or mode is rejected
timed out or partially failed shard responses fail closed

stop_conditions: cross-tenant result, missing or duplicated page-boundary identity, P99 or OpenSearch resource budget exceeds the approved baseline

tests: G1 signed cursor codec and HTTP repository protocol
G2 real OpenSearch search_after and PIT traversal
G3 page-boundary identity and tenant reconciliation
G4 fixed-scale cold and warm performance
G6 canary, rollback and PIT cleanup
evidence: candidate manifest, OpenSearch request profile, page-boundary identities, PIT inventory, HAR, trace, rollback and T+0/T+1/T+3/T+7 observations from immutable run_ids
